newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen pare JGB-driven gains, seen sideways.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen pare JGB-driven gains, seen sideways.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures remained well supported but failed to sustain their early gains on Tuesday after a Japanese government bond (JGB) futures rally fizzled, dealers said.

December JGBs hit a high of 126.14 partly on the back of a news agency report that the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s quarterly tankan survey would not show much improvement in business sentiment at small- and medium-sized firms, signalling the need for continued low interest rates.
The survey is due to be released on November 27.
But dealers said Euroyen futures were slow to follow the surge in JGBs, which came off just as quickly as they had risen.
"People found they might have over-reacted (to the report) and the JGBs came back down quite quickly," said a trader with a U.S. institution, adding that they would be supported at 125.10.
December JGBs ended at 125.39 against their previous 125.38.
A Japanese bank dealer said long positions had been accumulated at the 122.00 level and if that broke, the market could be in for a big move down.
The lead June Euroyen contract stood unchanged against its IMM close at 99.22 at 1125 GMT after hitting a high of 99.24.
The trader said it was likely to remain in a range of 99.19-99.24 ahead of the tankan.
"Although the market is looking to sell Euroyen a little bit after the recent rally, it's apparently being supported by reports like these," he said, referring to the news report on the tankan.
Eurodollar futures ended flat in skimpy trade as a lack of significant economic data or news kept most players out.
The March contract finished unchanged against its IMM close at 99.49 on volume of 2,110 lots.
